voice.refText: You wake up and discover you can pause time. 10 seconds once a day. At first, you use it for dumb things. You catch your falling coffee. You dodge your boss in the hallway.

Mother.describe: A warm, low female alto: a mother in her late fifties in her own kitchen. Unhurried and teasing, soft-spoken, a little husky, a light Filipino English lilt, love under every plain word.

Aunt one.describe: A sweet, chirpy female voice, a high mezzo: an aunt in her sixties. Fond and a little vague, delighted with her phone, a light Filipino English lilt.

Aunt two.describe: A grand, slow female alto: an aunt in her sixties. Gracious and dramatic, savouring every word, a light Filipino English lilt.

Bus kid.describe: A high, bright boy's voice, about eight years old. Curious and earnest, whispering loudly on a night bus.

Coworker.describe: A soft, low female voice, an alto: a call-centre worker in her twenties at four in the morning. A hushed whisper, protective and tired.

Best friend.describe: A bright, tired female mezzo: a woman of about thirty who works night shifts at a call centre. Quick and warm, a laugh close under the words, hoarse at the edges from talking all night, casual modern English.

Cousin.describe: A bright, sunny female soprano: a cousin in her twenties working abroad, waving into a phone camera. Cheerful and a little homesick, a light Filipino English lilt.

Manager.describe: A smooth, clipped male baritone: an office boss in his forties in a tie. Confident and transactional, quietly pleased with himself, every sentence a deal.

lines.text: Mother: Make a wish. A real one.
lines.say: [warm, teasing, shielding a candle] Make a wish. A real one.
lines.speaker: Mother

lines.text: Mother: What? What is it?
lines.say: [alarmed, leaning in, half a laugh] What? What is it?
lines.speaker: Mother

lines.text: That's what happens when a birthday wish is specific.
lines.say: [hushed, amused, close to the ear] That's what happens when a birthday wish is specific.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: So what if you could see who uses AI to text you? Everyone who did. Every time.
lines.say: [curious, leaning in on the question, the last four words slow] So what if you could see who uses AI to text you? Everyone who did. Every time.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Forty-one messages. Thirty-three dots. And the only one you'd have marked down for spelling is the only one a person typed.
lines.say: [dry, soft, the last clause landing] Forty-one messages. Thirty-three dots. And the only one you'd have marked down for spelling is the only one a person typed.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Your father. Eight months out on a cargo ship. Three words, one of them wrong, same as always.
lines.say: [tender, a small smile on the last three words] Your father. Eight months out on a cargo ship. Three words, one of them wrong, same as always.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: You've always graded people by their messages. Long means love. Short means busy. A typo means they couldn't be bothered.
lines.say: [warm, teasing, a confession on your behalf] You've always graded people by their messages. Long means love. Short means busy. A typo means they couldn't be bothered.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The rule. Every message you can read, in any app, from anyone, a text, a comment, a review: if a machine wrote it and a person only pressed send, or didn't even do that, it gets a small red dot.
lines.say: [clear, brisk, exact, each item a beat] The rule. Every message you can read, in any app, from anyone, a text, a comment, a review: if a machine wrote it and a person only pressed send, or didn't even do that, it gets a small red dot.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Only you see them. They are never wrong.
lines.say: [plain, certain] Only you see them. They are never wrong.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: But a dot says who wrote it. It never says why. Remember that.
lines.say: [measured, slower, the last two words almost a whisper] But a dot says who wrote it. It never says why. Remember that.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Mother: Dots? What dots?
lines.say: [puzzled, turning the phone over, mild] Dots? What dots?
lines.speaker: Mother

lines.text: Your father is one of about two million Filipinos working overseas. For a family like yours, the phone is where home is.
lines.say: [tender, steady, the fact said gently] Your father is one of about two million Filipinos working overseas. For a family like yours, the phone is where home is.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: You start writing him something long. Something worthy. After four words, the phone offers the rest. In grey.
lines.say: [warm, then slowing, the last two words cold] You start writing him something long. Something worthy. After four words, the phone offers the rest. In grey.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: You don't send it. Not yet. First you want to know who else.
lines.say: [quiet, a decision forming, a hook on the last three words] You don't send it. Not yet. First you want to know who else.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The landlord. Rent reminder, cold, two lines. No dot.
lines.say: [brisk, amused, surprised on no dot] The landlord. Rent reminder, cold, two lines. No dot.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Your boss. So proud of this team, a whole paragraph. Dot. Your sick day, noted. No dot. He typed the one you didn't want.
lines.say: [dry, a wince of a joke on the last sentence] Your boss. So proud of this team, a whole paragraph. Dot. Your sick day, noted. No dot. He typed the one you didn't want.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Your two aunts. Eleven messages this week, all between them.
lines.say: [amused, setting up] Your two aunts. Eleven messages this week, all between them.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Aunt one: Lovely.
lines.say: [pleased, reading her one word aloud as she types it] Lovely.
lines.speaker: Aunt one

lines.text: Aunt two: She writes so beautifully.
lines.say: [proud, moved, to nobody] She writes so beautifully.
lines.speaker: Aunt two

lines.text: Aunt one: Forgive me? For what?
lines.say: [baffled, indignant, to the phone] Forgive me? For what?
lines.speaker: Aunt one

lines.text: Nobody did anything. Two machines have fought and made up all week, and both aunts are proud of them.
lines.say: [deadpan, a laugh held under it] Nobody did anything. Two machines have fought and made up all week, and both aunts are proud of them.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The man from the dating app. A month of flirting, every line dotted. He has never typed you a word.
lines.say: [dry, then flat and a little hurt on the last sentence] The man from the dating app. A month of flirting, every line dotted. He has never typed you a word.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Then the pattern. The warm ones are dotted. The bare ones are short, late and misspelt.
lines.say: [slower, hurt, the floor tilting] Then the pattern. The warm ones are dotted. The bare ones are short, late and misspelt.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Your mother's eat first, every letter fixed by the phone: bare. Chosen words get a dot. Fixed letters don't.
lines.say: [fond, then exact] Your mother's eat first, every letter fixed by the phone: bare. Chosen words get a dot. Fixed letters don't.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: In a study this year, more than 1,300 Americans read a personal message. Told it was written by AI, they called the sender lazy and insincere. Told nothing, most never suspected.
lines.say: [clear, calm, the fact plain, a chill on the last sentence] In a study this year, more than thirteen hundred Americans read a personal message. Told it was written by AI, they called the sender lazy and insincere. Told nothing, most never suspected.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: And you agree with them. A machine can't mean it.
lines.say: [plain, certain, a wrong certainty] And you agree with them. A machine can't mean it.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: But here's problem one. You've checked everyone but the one you're afraid to.
lines.say: [leaning in, hushed, the last word soft] But here's problem one. You've checked everyone but the one you're afraid to.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Your best friend. Bea. Eleven years. The paragraph that made you cry this morning had a dot on it.
lines.say: [tender, slow, the last clause almost unwilling] Your best friend. Bea. Eleven years. The paragraph that made you cry this morning had a dot on it.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: You don't ask. Asking is accusing. You test: the one thing only she would know.
lines.say: [quiet, careful, a plan] You don't ask. Asking is accusing. You test: the one thing only she would know.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The day a goat got on your school bus and sat down next to her.
lines.say: [warm, a laugh under it] The day a goat got on your school bus and sat down next to her.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The first time in eleven years you've sent her two letters.
lines.say: [cold, clipped, quiet] The first time in eleven years you've sent her two letters.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Then you make the mistake every detective makes. You check your own pockets.
lines.say: [low, dry, a hook on the last sentence] Then you make the mistake every detective makes. You check your own pockets.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Your sent folder. A year back.
lines.say: [hushed, a held breath] Your sent folder. A year back.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Your thank-you to your boss. Dot. Your condolence to a coworker whose father died. Dot. Half of this morning's thank-yous. Dots.
lines.say: [flat, each dot a small blow, shame rising] Your thank-you to your boss. Dot. Your condolence to a coworker whose father died. Dot. Half of this morning's thank-yous. Dots.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Gmail has offered to write your replies since 2015, and to finish your sentences since 2018.
lines.say: [calm, exact, a fact that lands on you] Gmail has offered to write your replies since twenty fifteen, and to finish your sentences since twenty eighteen.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The detective is a suspect.
lines.say: [quiet, ashamed, a complete thought] The detective is a suspect.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: You typed that a year ago, after a fight with her. You forgot. The machine never did.
lines.say: [slow, hushed, the last sentence landing] You typed that a year ago, after a fight with her. You forgot. The machine never did.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: You switch every suggestion off.
lines.say: [clipped, hard] You switch every suggestion off.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: But here's problem two. You can't un-know what you are. So you become the opposite.
lines.say: [leaning in, low, a turn on the last sentence] But here's problem two. You can't un-know what you are. So you become the opposite.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: You type every word yourself now. Short. Late. Clumsy. Not a dot on you.
lines.say: [dry, brisk, a montage voice, a little proud] You type every word yourself now. Short. Late. Clumsy. Not a dot on you.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Hers get longer. Are we okay. Did I do something. I'm here, whenever. Dot. Dot. Dot.
lines.say: [mounting, each message a shade sadder, the dots flat] Hers get longer. Are we okay. Did I do something. I'm here, whenever. Dot. Dot. Dot.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The dots become a blade. You leave the aunts' chat. You block the man from the dating app.
lines.say: [hard, quick, ruthless] The dots become a blade. You leave the aunts' chat. You block the man from the dating app.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: You never see it.
lines.say: [quiet, bare, a little sad] You never see it.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Mother: Why so cold with everyone?
lines.say: [mild, worried, not turning round] Why so cold with everyone?
lines.speaker: Mother

lines.text: Your father. No dot. You don't call.
lines.say: [soft, guilty, slowing] Your father. No dot. You don't call.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The one person who never gets a dot is the one you keep not answering.
lines.say: [low, the hook quiet] The one person who never gets a dot is the one you keep not answering.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Mother: He never could spell. Look.
lines.say: [fond, a laugh in it, showing you] He never could spell. Look.
lines.speaker: Mother

lines.text: Mother: The card's not his. That is.
lines.say: [quiet, certain, touching the pen] The card's not his. That is.
lines.speaker: Mother

lines.text: Hallmark has printed greeting cards since 1915. For over a hundred years, people have signed their names under somebody else's words.
lines.say: [calm, thinking, the fact said gently] Hallmark has printed greeting cards since nineteen fifteen. For over a hundred years, people have signed their names under somebody else's words.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: And she kept every one, for three words in pen.
lines.say: [warm, slow on the last four words] And she kept every one, for three words in pen.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: A dot is a greeting card that hides the card.
lines.say: [thinking aloud, a complete thought] A dot is a greeting card that hides the card.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: But a card has a signature. A dot means they didn't even sign.
lines.say: [colder, certain, the wrong belief said plainly] But a card has a signature. A dot means they didn't even sign.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: So you decide to end it. Eleven years. To her face.
lines.say: [quiet, hard, a decision] So you decide to end it. Eleven years. To her face.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The night bus. Two in the morning. Her call centre is across the city.
lines.say: [hushed, tired, a city going by] The night bus. Two in the morning. Her call centre is across the city.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Bus kid: How do you spell sorry?
lines.say: [small, serious, tongue out, six years old] How do you spell sorry?
lines.speaker: Bus kid

lines.text: What limits a friendship is time. Every friendship costs time to keep.
lines.say: [calm, careful, the fact said close] What limits a friendship is time. Every friendship costs time to keep.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Twelve hours a night. For eleven years you graded her hours, and never asked where they came from.
lines.say: [quiet, the floor tilting, a little ashamed] Twelve hours a night. For eleven years you graded her hours, and never asked where they came from.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Coworker: Twelve hours. Don't wake her.
lines.say: [whispered, firm, kind] Twelve hours. Don't wake her.
lines.speaker: Coworker

lines.text: Best friend: You came?
lines.say: [half asleep, hoarse, disbelieving, glad] You came?
lines.speaker: Best friend

lines.text: She was keeping you with the only hours she had left: the ones she was asleep for.
lines.say: [tender, slow, a complete thought] She was keeping you with the only hours she had left: the ones she was asleep for.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: You said a dot means they didn't even sign. She signed a year ago.
lines.say: [quiet, the break landing, no triumph] You said a dot means they didn't even sign. She signed a year ago.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Her side. Your week. Ok. Fine. K. Not a dot on them. All honest. All read as you leaving.
lines.say: [flat, each word a small blow, hurt on the last sentence] Her side. Your week. Ok. Fine. K. Not a dot on them. All honest. All read as you leaving.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Then her drafts. Twenty she never sent. Four in the morning. Her own thumbs. Misspelt. Bare.
lines.say: [hushed, slow, every fragment heavier] Then her drafts. Twenty she never sent. Four in the morning. Her own thumbs. Misspelt. Bare.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Best friend: I didn't know how to say it right.
lines.say: [small, tired, ashamed] I didn't know how to say it right.
lines.speaker: Best friend

lines.text: You'd have believed every one. She never sent them. Not good enough. You taught her that. Long means love.
lines.say: [hurt, quiet, the last three words bitter] You'd have believed every one. She never sent them. Not good enough. You taught her that. Long means love.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Best friend: Eleven years, and you sent me ok.
lines.say: [hurt, a laugh breaking in it, not angry] Eleven years, and you sent me ok.
lines.speaker: Best friend

lines.text: And then you look up, and it was never just your phone.
lines.say: [low, widening, a hook] And then you look up, and it was never just your phone.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The restaurant downstairs. Five-star reviews. A dot on every one.
lines.say: [wide, wry] The restaurant downstairs. Five-star reviews. A dot on every one.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Cousin: Thank you all so much. I love you all.
lines.say: [bright, tearful, waving at a camera] Thank you all so much. I love you all.
lines.speaker: Cousin

lines.text: Four hundred comments under your cousin's video. A field of red.
lines.say: [flat, turning grim] Four hundred comments under your cousin's video. A field of red.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: At work, you start calling it. That review's fake. Those are bots. Right every time.
lines.say: [brisk, sharp, a little gleeful, a shade of warning on the last three words] At work, you start calling it. That review's fake. Those are bots. Right every time.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: One security company estimated that in 2024, bots, good and bad, passed people: 51 per cent of everything on the web, for the first time in a decade.
lines.say: [clear, exact, a touch of awe] One security company estimated that in twenty twenty-four, bots, good and bad, passed people: fifty-one per cent of everything on the web, for the first time in a decade.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Then your boss's message. A bonus bigger than a year's pay. Mark which of a rival campaign's supporters are real. It arrives with a dot.
lines.say: [quiet, tempted, then dry on the last sentence] Then your boss's message. A bonus bigger than a year's pay. Mark which of a rival campaign's supporters are real. It arrives with a dot.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Your father, under your mother's homecoming plans. No dot. The only bare bubble in twenty.
lines.say: [soft, a lump in it] Your father, under your mother's homecoming plans. No dot. The only bare bubble in twenty.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: If a machine wrote it but they meant it, does it still count? Because a dot never says why.
lines.say: [the question put straight to you, slow, then plain] If a machine wrote it but they meant it, does it still count? Because a dot never says why.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Sell what you see, and every fake gets a price on its head. So does every night-shift worker who let a machine finish a sentence. Keep it, and every tired person keeps their machine.
lines.say: [even, both sides weighed, no hint of the answer] Sell what you see, and every fake gets a price on its head. So does every night-shift worker who let a machine finish a sentence. Keep it, and every tired person keeps their machine.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Manager: There's nothing there.
lines.say: [flat, puzzled, handing it back] There's nothing there.
lines.speaker: Manager

lines.text: You walk out.
lines.say: [quiet, a door closing] You walk out.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: You need to see how big it is.
lines.say: [hushed, breath in it, climbing] You need to see how big it is.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Around the turn of the century, the Philippines was called the texting capital of the world. A few years later: over a billion texts a day.
lines.say: [awe, slow, the number landing alone] Around the turn of the century, the Philippines was called the texting capital of the world. A few years later: over a billion texts a day.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Every lit window is a chat. From up here, you can see the dots.
lines.say: [hushed, wide, a little afraid] Every lit window is a chat. From up here, you can see the dots.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Now take away the dotted ones.
lines.say: [very quiet, a dare to yourself] Now take away the dotted ones.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Those are the people typing. Everyone else is asleep, or working, or scared of getting it wrong.
lines.say: [awe, hushed, tender on the last clause] Those are the people typing. Everyone else is asleep, or working, or scared of getting it wrong.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Your phone buzzes. A calendar reminder you never set.
lines.say: [puzzled, quiet, a hook] Your phone buzzes. A calendar reminder you never set.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: You delete it. At nine you go anyway.
lines.say: [dry, then a decision, warm] You delete it. At nine you go anyway.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Best friend: You booked this?
lines.say: [surprised, wary, hopeful] You booked this?
lines.speaker: Best friend

lines.text: Best friend: ...Neither did I.
lines.say: [slow, a dawning, almost a laugh] Neither did I.
lines.speaker: Best friend

lines.text: The best conversation of your year. Midnight, three months ago, the night you made up after the fight.
lines.say: [wonder, slow, fond on the last clause] The best conversation of your year. Midnight, three months ago, the night you made up after the fight.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Every line. Both sides. Dotted.
lines.say: [flat, each word alone, the floor gone] Every line. Both sides. Dotted.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Her instruction. Yours. Two machines, told the same thing by two people who were asleep, booked a cafe.
lines.say: [wonder, a laugh starting under it] Her instruction. Yours. Two machines, told the same thing by two people who were asleep, booked a cafe.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: In a 2023 study, people who suspected their chat partner was using AI-suggested replies judged them more harshly. But actually using them made the conversation warmer and closer. The use never hurt the conversation. The suspicion did.
lines.say: [calm, exact, the last two sentences slow and plain] In a twenty twenty-three study, people who suspected their chat partner was using AI-suggested replies judged them more harshly. But actually using them made the conversation warmer and closer. The use never hurt the conversation. The suspicion did.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: You said a machine can't mean it.
lines.say: [quiet, the old line held up to the light] You said a machine can't mean it.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Nobody wrote it. Both of you meant it.
lines.say: [warm, slow, a complete thought] Nobody wrote it. Both of you meant it.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Your father's message. Two weeks old. You were going to write something long. Something worthy.
lines.say: [quiet, guilty, the last two words a little mocking of yourself] Your father's message. Two weeks old. You were going to write something long. Something worthy.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Three words. One of them wrong. Your thumb goes to fix it.
lines.say: [hushed, slow, a held breath on the last sentence] Three words. One of them wrong. Your thumb goes to fix it.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: You leave it.
lines.say: [very soft, the breath let go] You leave it.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Send. No dot.
lines.say: [quiet, bare] Send. No dot.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Mother: He never could spell.
lines.say: [fond, not turning round, a smile in it] He never could spell.
lines.speaker: Mother

lines.text: No paragraph. No grade. No fix.
lines.say: [warm, each fragment lighter] No paragraph. No grade. No fix.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Tomorrow someone will send you three words with a mistake in them. Read them twice. Nobody else could have sent them.
lines.say: [tender, close, a complete thought on the last sentence] Tomorrow someone will send you three words with a mistake in them. Read them twice. Nobody else could have sent them.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: So, would you fix the typo? Tell us in the comments. And if you'd have done the same, hit like and subscribe.
lines.say: [warm, direct, a small smile] So, would you fix the typo? Tell us in the comments. And if you'd have done the same, hit like and subscribe.
lines.speaker: narrator
